title: hotfix: add backoff hysteresis to SLO enforcer to prevent thrashing during regional failover
author: Priya Kothari
description: Context: During the 2026-02-17 regional failover incident we observed the SLO enforcer make aggressive backoff decisions in multiple regions concurrently which triggered cascading load-shedding and prolonged recovery. Root cause: a subtle race between the backoff state machine and the regional-failover handler that allowed rapid oscillation (backoff -> recover -> immediate backoff) without any hysteresis, combined with an ordering issue where newly-activated failover policies reset transient counters. This PR introduces deterministic hysteresis to the backoff decision path and a small ordering fix to ensure failover activation does not clear the recent-backoff window. Summary of changes: 1) add a hysteresis window (configurable, default 45s) to the SLO enforcer so that once a backoff is applied the enforcer requires sustained healthy signals for the hysteresis window before lifting backoff; 2) change failover activation path to set failover-active flag before mutating transient counters to avoid clearing recent-backoff state; 3) expose metrics for backoff hysteresis transitions and a per-region backoff_stability counter for faster debugging; 4) add unit and integration regression tests that reproduce the oscillation pattern seen in prod; 5) small docs/operational note for on-call runbook. Checklist: - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration/regression test reproducer - [x] metrics emitted and dashboard update requested - [x] rollout and rollback plan included - [x] automated canary to main for 2h post-merge Testing & verification: locally reproduced the oscillation with the synthetic failover harness, ran end-to-end against the canary environment (us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 failover scenario) and measured a 6x reduction in backoff churn and removal of repeated load-shedding events during recovery windows. Observability: new metrics slo_enforcer.hysteresis_entered, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_exited, slo_enforcer.backoff_stability_count. Deploy notes: squash-merge to main, canary for 2 hours in non-peak traffic with SRE monitoring on duty; if regressions are observed revert the release via rollback tag (instructions in deploy/rollback.md). Related: ENG-4621 (incident follow-up), ENG-4623 (longer-term enforcer rewrite).
